## Summary

- Adds `quartz/components/Transcript.tsx`: a collapsible `<details>` block that renders episode captions with EN/ZH language tab toggle
- Reads `captionEn` and `captionZh` frontmatter paths at build time via `allFiles` lookup — no runtime fetch needed
- Shows tabs only when both languages exist; gracefully renders nothing when neither frontmatter field is set
- Exports `Transcript` from `quartz/components/index.ts`
- Registers the component in `quartz.layout.ts` `afterBody` for episode pages (before Comments)
- Creates `content/captions/.gitkeep` to track the captions directory (populated by the upcoming caption-workflow)

## Frontmatter convention (opt-in, no existing files modified)

```yaml
captionEn: /captions/ep01.en.md
captionZh: /captions/ep01.zh.md
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify no TypeScript errors in layout or component files
- [ ] Build site locally; episode pages with no caption frontmatter render normally (Transcript block absent)
- [ ] After caption-workflow PR merges, add `captionEn`/`captionZh` to an episode and confirm transcript renders with correct tab switching

Closes #40

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue

- PR #41 adds `quartz/components/Transcript.tsx`: a collapsible `<details>` block that renders episode captions with an EN/ZH language tab toggle.
- Caption files are resolved at build time via `allFiles` lookup using `captionEn`/`captionZh` frontmatter paths — no runtime fetch needed.
- The component opts-in gracefully: it renders nothing when neither frontmatter field is set and shows the tab bar only when both languages exist.
- This is the infrastructure half of the caption system; the caption-workflow PR (GH Actions download + translate) is still pending.
- The PR went through three commits: initial implementation → fix pass (addressed two prior BLOCKINGs) → revert of an `ignorePatterns` addition that was itself a BLOCKING finding.

## Review

Both prior BLOCKING findings are fully resolved in the current HEAD. Two WARNING-level issues remain in the `afterDOMLoaded` inline script: missing SPA cleanup registration and an incomplete ARIA keyboard navigation pattern.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Missing `window.addCleanup` in `afterDOMLoaded` | WARNING | Tab click listeners are not registered with the Quartz SPA cleanup contract, breaking the established pattern and leaving abandoned listeners on navigation. |
| ARIA tab widget keyboard-inaccessible | WARNING | `role="tablist"` / `role="tab"` are declared correctly, but `tabindex` management and `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` key handling are absent — keyboard-only users cannot switch transcript languages. |
| Caption files unguarded from index/search/RSS | INFO | No `draft: true` or path-scoped exclusion on caption files; must be enforced in the caption-workflow PR before real caption files land. |
| Hardcoded panel IDs | INFO | `id="panel-en"` / `id="panel-zh"` would collide if more than one `Transcript` were ever rendered per page. Not a concern today. |
| Dark-mode CSS rule is a no-op | INFO | `:root[saved-theme="dark"] .transcript { border-color: var(--lightgray) }` duplicates the default value; cosmetic debt only. |

## Progress

- **RESOLVED (BLOCKING):** `renderContent` split bug (`/\n\n+/` → `/\n+/`) and double HTML-entity escaping fixed in commit `2c77295` via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
- **RESOLVED (BLOCKING):** `ignorePatterns: ["captions"]` addition (which silently broke `allFiles` lookup) reverted in commit `84d935d`.
- **RESOLVED (WARNING, prior round):** Full ARIA tab semantics applied — `role="tablist"`, `role="tab"`, `aria-selected`, `aria-controls`, `role="tabpanel"`.
- **Thread resolved:** Stale `quartz.config.ts` thread (`PRRT_kwDOQ106186CRtIw`) on the `ignorePatterns` finding was unresolved in the UI despite the revert; resolved now.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Missing `window.addCleanup` in `afterDOMLoaded`</summary>

**Cause:** The `afterDOMLoaded` script attaches click listeners to each `.transcript-tab` element inside an arrow function passed to `tab.addEventListener`, but never calls `window.addCleanup`. Every other Quartz component that registers DOM listeners follows the SPA cleanup contract: `spa.inline.ts` (lines 84–86) calls all registered cleanup functions before replacing the DOM on navigation.

**Candidate solutions:**
```js
// Hoist handler so it can be referenced in cleanup
const handler = () => {
  // existing click body
}
tab.addEventListener("click", handler)
window.addCleanup(() => tab.removeEventListener("click", handler))
```

**Comments:** In practice, listeners on replaced DOM nodes are GC'd anyway — this is not a functional memory leak today, but it breaks the codebase contract and will mislead contributors who copy the pattern.

</details>

<details>
<summary>ARIA tab widget keyboard-inaccessible</summary>

**Cause:** The [WAI-ARIA Tabs pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/) requires `tabindex="0"` on the active tab and `tabindex="-1"` on inactive tabs, plus `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` key events on the tab bar to move focus. Without this, keyboard-only users can reach the tab bar via Tab but cannot switch languages without a mouse — affecting transcript comprehension.

**Candidate solutions:**

In JSX, add initial `tabIndex` props:
```tsx
<button role="tab" aria-selected="true" tabIndex={0} ...>EN</button>
<button role="tab" aria-selected="false" tabIndex={-1} ...>ZH</button>
```

In `afterDOMLoaded`, add arrow-key handler (and toggle `tabindex` in the click handler):
```js
const keyHandler = (e) => {
  const tabs = [...bar.querySelectorAll(".transcript-tab")]
  const idx = tabs.indexOf(document.activeElement)
  if (e.key === "ArrowRight" && idx < tabs.length - 1) tabs[idx + 1].focus()
  if (e.key === "ArrowLeft" && idx > 0) tabs[idx - 1].focus()
}
bar.addEventListener("keydown", keyHandler)
window.addCleanup(() => bar.removeEventListener("keydown", keyHandler))
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Caption files unguarded from index/search/RSS</summary>

**Cause:** Caption markdown files have no `draft: true` frontmatter and are not excluded from `ContentIndex` configuration. The current `.gitkeep` placeholder adds no indexable content, but real caption files (populated by the caption-workflow PR) will appear in search results, sitemaps, and RSS feeds unless a guard is put in place.

**Candidate solutions:** Add a path-scoped filter in `ContentIndex` configuration in the caption-workflow PR, or attach `draft: true` to all caption file templates.

**Comments:** This is explicitly a future-PR concern and the PR description already calls it out. No action needed here.

</details>
